## Decision ledger

**(a) Who controls the source?**
`chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener` (background.js L831) is the entry point. The message comes from a *web page* whose origin matches `externally_connectable.matches` (`*://*.custom-cursor.com/*`, `*://custom-cursor.com/*`). There is **no `sender.id` check and no `sender.origin`/`sender.url` check** anywhere in the listener — only `request.action` is switched on. So `request.value` (and `request.key`) are web-content-controlled, constrained only by the connectable web origins (XSS/subdomain-takeover on those origins suffices).

**(b) Source-to-sink path**
L831 `onMessageExternal` → L833 `case "set"` → L834 `let obj = {}` → L835 `obj[request.key] = request.value` → L836 `chrome.storage.local.set(obj, ...)`. The tainted object is passed directly to the privileged storage write on the very next line. The sink is unbroken.

**(c) Security-relevant argument**
The attacker controls *both* the storage key (`request.key`) and the stored value (`request.value`). `chrome.storage.local.set(obj)` therefore writes fully attacker-chosen persist

sourceReachability.browserFacts: externally_connectable controls which page origins/extension IDs can call the listener. Only a browser-supplied sender.id comparison to a fixed extension ID is an unforgeable IPC boundary. Origin/url restrictions and manifest matches reduce scope but are not proof that attacker input is impossible.

browserTrustRules: sender.id is browser-populated and only a fixed-ID allowlist is an unforgeable inter-extension trust boundary.
event.origin/window.location.origin and message action/type fields are attacker-satisfiable in a page-to-content-script bridge.

chrome.action/browserAction badge, title, icon, and chrome.notifications UI state are extension/browser authority; attacker-controlled operative fields are TP, not harmless presentation. Verify the value reaches the API argument.
A source/sink match in an import statement, comment, dead code, or an unrelated action branch is not a data-flow proof.
For chrome.tabs.create/windows.create/downloads/fetch/WebSocket, verify that the tainted value controls the URL/body/options actually consumed by the API.
